short_description: A two-session (test-retest) mouse-tracking go/no-go paradigm measuring continuous cursor-control dynamics and stopping behaviour in 26 healthy adults.
long_description: Participants completed a go/no-go task in which a cursor was moved toward one of two target boxes using the mouse. On go trials they moved the cursor into the target box as fast and accurately as possible; on no-go trials they had to stop the ongoing movement. The raw per-trial mouse-trajectory samples were scored with the delivered R script, which detects target-box entry and no-go stopping to produce per-trial reaction time, stopping time, accuracy, path length, velocity and acceleration. The study was run twice per participant (test-retest) to support inter-session reliability (ICC) estimates. The paper (Mahesan et al., 2026, bioRxiv) reports the behavioural and kinematic results.
background: The study uses mouse tracking to measure continuous control and inhibitory behaviour in a go/no-go task, in line with the paper's aim of characterising stopping dynamics and their reliability across repeated testing. The paper (Mahesan et al., 2026, bioRxiv) describes the task, participants and analysis; the present description records the restructured BEEHub data, the scored derivation and the PI-declared outcomes.
procedure: Participants performed a go/no-go mouse-tracking task in two sessions (test-retest). Each session comprised 15 blocks: two practice blocks (go-only, then go/nogo practice, 18 trials each) followed by 13 experimental blocks (five go-only and eight go/nogo blocks). On each trial a stimulus appeared and, on go trials, the participant moved the mouse cursor into the target box; on no-go trials the participant stopped the movement. Inter-trial intervals were randomised between 0.5 and 1.0 s. Raw per-trial mouse samples were scored offline (target-box entry and no-go stopping detection) to produce per-trial outcome columns.
trial_structure: 611 trials per session (measured, identical across all complete participants), broken down as 506 go, 100 no-go and 5 'n/a' (practice/blank) rows. Blocks per session: 15 total, of which 2 are practice (block 1 go-only, block 2 go/nogo practice, 18 trials each) and 13 experimental (5 go-only blocks of 18 trials, 8 go/nogo blocks of 60 trials). The 506 go rows comprise 90 from go-only blocks plus 480 from go/nogo blocks; the 100 no-go rows plus 5 practice 'n/a' rows account for the remainder. The measured 611 rows match the design derived from block_sequence.xlsx exactly.
design: Two-session test-retest within-participants design. 26 participants; sessions a and b map to ses-01 and ses-02 (a precedes b by acquisition date). 24 participants have both sessions; participants 2 and 4 have ses-01 only, giving 50 data files. Outcome columns were derived per trial from raw mouse-trajectory samples; inter-session reliability was to be assessed with ICC on the declared outcome measures.
